extracted.intended_audience: new GAP users (mathematicians/programmers) who want to learn to use the GAP system
extracted.subtask_description: A hands-on tutorial for interactively using the GAP computer-algebra system: starting/stopping sessions, basic syntax, writing and loading code, objects/variables, functions, lists/records, domains, attributes, methods, and using packages/help. Geared to users who have just started GAP and want worked examples to learn the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: License and distribution terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Most parts of the GAP distribution (including the core) are distributed under the GNU General Public License; details available at https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl.html or the file GPL in the etc directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Copyright and License reference for full details; know that GAP is free/open and that parts have various copyrights and contributors. Check CHANGES.md for release changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: System composition: core + packages + data + docs
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP consists of a kernel (C), a large GAP-language library, group-theoretical data libraries, and documentation; additional functionality is provided by self-contained packages which include code and docs and can be loaded with LoadPackage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that packages may be OS-dependent, may load automatically if present, and are recommended for extended functionality; package docs are treated like core docs once loaded. See Packages/Using and Developing GAP on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start GAP by running gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically start GAP by typing gap at the OS prompt; banner can be suppressed with -b option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To end a session type quit; (do not omit semicolon) or use CTRL-D on some systems; CTRL-C twice within a second also ends GAP. Follow INSTALL and platform-specific instructions if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate statements with a semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP input statements should be terminated with a semicolon to indicate command completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting the semicolon and pressing RETURN leads to a partial prompt > until the command is completed; type the missing semicolon on the next line. Use semicolons to avoid unintended evaluation; double semicolon prevents printing of the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double semicolon suppresses printed result
rubrics_metrics.description: Appending ;; to a statement executes it but suppresses printing of the returned object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for assignments and commands where you don't want the object echoed (e.g., w:=2;;). Prevents clutter in interactive sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace is mostly insignificant
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces, TABs and RETURNs are usually insignificant for GAP input meaning; identifiers and keywords must not contain whitespace and sometimes whitespace is required to separate tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whitespace to format complex commands for readability; be aware that keywords composed of letters (e.g., mod) require surrounding whitespace (e.g., 17 mod 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments begin with # and run to end of line
rubrics_metrics.description: Use # to start a comment; the rest of the line is ignored by GAP and treated as whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments extensively in source files and examples to explain input/output to human readers; comments are ignored during execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifiers and assignment syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifiers are sequences of letters and digits with at least one letter (e.g., abc, a0bc1, 123a). Assignment is done with := and there must be no whitespace between : and =.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse := with = (equality test). Keywords (like quit) must not be used as identifiers. Identifiers are case-sensitive (a1 and A1 differ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global library variable naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Every global variable name in the GAP library starts with a capital letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose user variable names starting with a lowercase letter to avoid attempting to overwrite predefined variables; most predefined variables are read-only and attempts to change them will error.

rubrics_metrics.name: last, last2, last3 store recent returned objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever GAP prints an object it assigns it to the variable last; there are also last2 and last3 for earlier results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use last to recover an unassigned result (e.g., a:= last;). Helpful during interactive experimentation when you forgot to assign a result.

rubrics_metrics.name: NamesGVars() and NamesUserGVars() for inspecting variables
rubrics_metrics.description: NamesGVars() lists all GAP variables (many predefined); NamesUserGVars() lists variables defined by the user in the current session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to get an overview of session state. Example: NamesUserGVars() might return ["a","w"].

rubrics_metrics.name: Values vs identity: IsIdenticalObj and = semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP distinguishes object identity (IsIdenticalObj) from mathematical equality (=). Objects can be equal mathematically without being identical in memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IsIdenticalObj(obj1,obj2) to test identity. Understand that different GAP objects may represent the same mathematical element (especially for composite objects like lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects are typed, identifiers are not
rubrics_metrics.description: Types belong to objects, not to identifiers; an identifier points to an object and can later point to objects of different types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful in code that variable names do not have inherent types; ensure runtime behavior matches expectations by checking object types if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions and procedures: side effects vs return values
rubrics_metrics.description: Most functions return objects; some functions (procedures) produce side effects (e.g., Print) and may not return useful objects; some both change arguments and return objects (e.g., Sortex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which functions are pure vs procedural; use Print with explicit newline characters ("\n") since Print does not append a line break by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define simple functions with maps-to operator ->
rubrics_metrics.description: Use x -> expression to define small functions inline (e.g., cubed:= x -> x^3;).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more complicated or multi-argument functions, use the full function ... end form explained in Section 4.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read input from files using Read
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Read(path) to load GAP source code from a file; supply absolute or relative path names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer editing larger programs in files and loading them rather than typing interactively; comments in files are preserved for human readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive REPL behaviour and editing keys
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP runs a read-evaluate-print loop. Line editing (DELETE/BACKSPACE, CTRL-B, CTRL-F, CTRL-P, CTRL-E) works in the prompt; syntax errors show location with ^ and may enter break loops (brk> etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stuck at a partial prompt, type semicolons until normal prompt returns. Use break loop commands (quit; or CTRL-D) to leave nested breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator classes, precedence, and parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP supports arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators; precedence rules apply and can be overridden with parentheses. The exponentiation operator is ^, negation unary -, mod is a keyword requiring whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with spacing around letter-based operators (mod). Use parentheses to make intentions explicit and avoid precedence mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutation syntax and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutations use cycle notation (e.g., (1,2,3)) and support multiplication, inverse via ^-1, image-of notation caret (2^(1,2,3)), and conjugation (p^q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize with caret operator's multiple uses (power, image, conjugation) to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters and string literals
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are entered as single-quoted literals (e.g., 'a', '*') and can be compared; there are no operators defined for characters beyond comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characters and strings where appropriate; consult Strings and Characters chapter for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the help system with ?[book:][?]topic
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP includes an indexed online help system accessible from the prompt with ? queries; ?book: restricts to a book, ?? does substring searches, and ?topic may list multiple matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ?books to list books and names. Use ?Ref: The Help System for full command list; help can be viewed via pager, browser or PDF viewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send bug reports to support@gap-system.org with session excerpt and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: For bugs not suitable for the forum, email support@gap-system.org with a short self-contained excerpt of a GAP session (input and output), reason why it's a bug, machine type, OS, compiler (if UNIX/Linux), and GAP version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this minimal reproducible example and environment speeds diagnosis. Also send a brief message upon installing GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in GAP Forum (subscribe before posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAP Forum is the email discussion list for comments/questions about GAP; you must subscribe before posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements such as new releases are posted there; use the forum for community-wide issues and discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the correct form of citation for GAP when publishing scientific results obtained using GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to documentation or website for the recommended citation text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists as primary composite data structure; sets as special lists
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP represents sets as lists without holes or duplicates and ordered by <; lists are fundamental and many math structures are introduced from lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand plain lists, identical lists, immutability issues (Sections 3.1–3.3), and special list-like types (ranges, vectors, matrices, records) before manipulating higher structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutability and identity pitfalls for composite objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite objects such as lists may have different GAP object representations for mathematically equal elements; IsIdenticalObj detects identity differences. Some functions may mutate objects (change in place).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when relying on object identity in algorithms; learn which operations mutate (in-place) and which return new objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domains, subdomains, and SubsomethingNC naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Many functions return subdomains of arguments; functions suffixed NC (no check) like SubsomethingNC(D, gens) skip domain containment checks when caller is sure the result lies in D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NC variants for performance when you are certain of containment; understand domain constructors, closures, and changing structures in Chapter 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes are getter/setter/tester triples
rubrics_metrics.description: Every attribute in GAP is represented by a getter, a setter and a tester: the getter consults the tester and either computes (real-work getter), stores (setter), and returns a value, or returns a stored system getter value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute getters may have multiple methods; the setter does nothing if a value is already stored. Example getter pseudocode is provided. Learn naming convention: SetXxx and HasXxx are setter/tester names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Once set, attribute values are immutable
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the value of an attribute for an object has been stored, it cannot be reset; the setter is implemented to do nothing if tester returns true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on changing stored attribute values; to alter attributes you must create new objects or rely on methods that compute without storing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties (boolean attributes) and filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean-valued attributes are properties; their getters and testers are filters. Filters are implemented as bits in a boolean list per object and can be combined with and to form compound filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filters are cheap to test and are central to method selection; use KnownPropertiesOfObject/KnownTruePropertiesOfObject to inspect them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method selection uses required filters and prefers most specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Each installed method for an operation/attribute has a required filter (possibly composed of simple filters). GAP selects among applicable methods the one whose required filter combines the most simple filters (i.e., most specific).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design methods with appropriate required filters; expect GAP to prefer more specialized methods for efficiency. If a method cannot compute, it should call TryNextMethod() to delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: TryNextMethod behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicable method cannot compute a result, it should call TryNextMethod(), and GAP will try the next applicable method in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for methods that include mandatory tests (e.g., solvability) and may fail for some inputs; allows chaining algorithms of differing specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate methods and true methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate methods run automatically when a filter/attribute value changes (e.g., derivations from known size); true methods implement logical implications between filters and are even cheaper bookkeeping rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate methods can trigger additional deductions (e.g., Feit–Thompson parity trick for IsSolvableGroup). True methods set filters with simple logical implications (IsGroup and IsCyclic => IsSolvableGroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations may have per-argument required filters and family relations
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-argument operations a required filter can be specified for each argument; methods may also require a relation between arguments expressed via families (e.g., ConjugateGroup requires element family matching group's element family).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of families (PermutationsFamily, CollectionsFamily) and that operands from incompatible families prevent method application (e.g., FreeGroup elements from distinct families cannot be multiplied).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introspection utilities: ApplicableMethod, TraceMethods, TraceImmediateMethods, UntraceMethods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ApplicableMethod(opr,[args],0,nr) to see which method(s) are applicable; TraceMethods([ops]) logs method selection; TraceImmediateMethods(true) logs immediate methods; UntraceMethods disables tracing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tracing and ApplicableMethod to debug method dispatch and to understand which methods are chosen and in what order; Useful for debugging NoMethodFound errors.
